claims.text: Rapid solidification produces a homogeneous metastable solid solution in the proposed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy.
Mg is uniformly dissolved in the initial rapidly solidified solid solution.
Subsequent thermal exposure causes Mg to segregate or exsolve from the metastable solid solution.
Segregated Mg nucleates and grows as Mg-rich intermetallic phases during thermal aging.
Mg-rich intermetallic compounds preferentially form at sites such as grain boundaries.
The Mg-rich intermetallic phases modify the local surface chemistry or electrochemical characteristics of the alloy.
Mg-rich intermetallic phases promote or catalyze formation of a protective oxide scale at high temperature.
Intermetallic-induced changes in surface electrochemistry enhance passivation in corrosive environments.
Formation of a more protective oxide scale improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Thermally aged samples will contain Mg-rich intermetallic compounds that are absent or less developed in the non-aged baseline.
Thermally aged samples will have lower corrosion rates than non-aged samples.
Thermally aged samples will form a more stable and protective high-temperature oxide layer than non-aged samples.
The controlled comparison will use identical rapidly solidified samples, with one set retained as-solidified and the other thermally aged.
The alloy density will be kept below 6 g/cm3.
Thermal aging will be restricted so that full equilibrium decomposition does not occur.
